title: Why King Zedekiah Secretly Asked Jeremiah for the Truth
paragraphs: Why King Zedekiah Secretly Asked Jeremiah for the Truth
The walls of Jerusalem had not fully collapsed yet.
The priests were still performing rituals.
The officials still wore their robes.
The king still sat on a throne.
But underneath the gold… Judah was already dying.
And deep inside the palace, a terrified king was secretly searching for a prophet he publicly refused to obey.
This is not merely the story of a weak ruler.
This is the story of every person who already knows the truth… but is afraid of what obedience will cost.

“Then Zedekiah the king sent and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him into the third entry that is in the house of the LORD: and the king said unto Jeremiah, I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.”
That verse feels heavy when you truly understand it.
Because Zedekiah did not ask Jeremiah publicly.
Away from the people influencing him.
He wanted truth… but not exposure.
He wanted clarity… but not surrender.
He wanted God’s voice… without God’s consequences.
And millions are still doing the exact same thing today.
Some people secretly watch sermons at night after spending all day pretending they do not care about God.
Some secretly pray after publicly living rebellious lives.
Some secretly know their relationship is sinful.
Some secretly know they are destroying themselves.
Some secretly know God has been warning them for years.
But like Zedekiah… they fear people more than they fear the Lord.
That is where this story becomes terrifyingly personal.

The Hebrew behind Jeremiah’s warnings carries the weight of covenant judgment. Jeremiah repeatedly declared that Babylon would conquer Jerusalem because Judah had violated God’s covenant through idolatry, injustice, bloodshed, and rebellion.
“If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire…”
The Hebrew phrase for “thy soul shall live” is:
This was mercy being offered in the middle of judgment.
God was still extending an escape.
Because fear of people can make cowards out of kings.
“And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid…”
That sentence exposes the entire tragedy.
The Hebrew word used here is:
It means to dread, fear, or live in terror.
He feared what people would think.
And because he feared man more than God… he lost both.
This is exactly why Proverbs 29:25 says:
“The fear of man bringeth a snare.”
Something that slowly tightens around your life.
Zedekiah was trapped long before Babylon broke the walls.
And some people reading this understand exactly what that feels like.
You know God has been convicting you.
But you are terrified of losing relationships.
Terrified of letting go of sin.
Terrified of becoming “too serious” about Jesus.
So you keep God in secret compartments.
He kept consulting Jeremiah privately while publicly refusing to fully obey.
And eventually the clock ran out.
Zedekiah watched his sons slaughtered before his eyes.
The last thing he ever saw was judgment.
“And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah…”
Because it did not have to happen.
This was not the destruction of a man who never heard truth.
This was the destruction of a man who repeatedly heard truth… but delayed obedience.
That is one of the most dangerous spiritual conditions possible.
Hearing truth without surrender hardens the heart.
The New Testament echoes this warning powerfully.
Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον
“Ginesthe de poiētai logou kai mē akroatai monon.”
“Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.”
The word “ἀκροαταὶ” (akroatai) refers to passive listeners.
And modern Christianity is filled with people secretly asking Jeremiah for truth while refusing to fully obey God publicly.
They love conviction as long as it stays emotional.
But conviction is supposed to lead somewhere.
This is what makes Jeremiah such a painful prophet.
He was hated because he refused to alter God’s message.
And Zedekiah kept bouncing between what felt good and what was true.
Many people do not want truth.
But the real Word of God does not merely comfort.
“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword…”
The Word of God exposes what we try to hide.
That is why Zedekiah kept meeting Jeremiah in secret.
And maybe that is why this story is hitting your spirit right now.
Because deep down… you already know.
You know what God has been convicting you about.
You know what you keep postponing.
You know the conversations you avoid.
You know the surrender you fear.
You know the sin you defend.
You know the wounds you hide behind sarcasm, pride, lust, anger, addiction, ambition, or distraction.
And still… Jesus stands ready to forgive.
That is the part many people miss.
Jeremiah’s warnings were severe, but God kept extending mercy.
The Lord kept sending prophets because He desired repentance.
Judgment was never His first desire.
“I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live.”
This is the heartbeat of repentance.
And this is where the Gospel becomes breathtaking.
Because where Zedekiah failed… Jesus succeeded.
Jesus stood silent before mockers and still obeyed unto death.
Jesus established an eternal Kingdom through the cross.
The Gospel is not merely a lesson about ancient kings.
It is the rescue of spiritually collapsing people.
Jesus Christ stepped into our rebellion and carried the judgment we deserved.
“But he was wounded for our transgressions…”
Christ was crushed so sinners could return.
That means your story does not have to end like Zedekiah’s.
You do not have to keep secretly asking for truth while publicly resisting God.
Because delayed obedience is still disobedience.
And hidden conviction eventually becomes visible destruction if ignored long enough.
But mercy is still reaching for you.
That is why you are reading this.
God is still calling people back before the walls collapse.
The terrifying thing about Zedekiah is not that he asked for the truth.
It is that he heard it clearly… and still refused to fully obey.
Do not let that become your story.
Some people are one warning away from surrender.
Others are one step away from collapse.
One day the hidden conversations in your soul will become visible in your life.
Bakit Palihim na Humingi si Haring Zedekias ng Katotohanan kay Jeremias
Hindi pa ganap na bumabagsak ang mga pader ng Jerusalem.
Patuloy pa rin ang mga pari sa kanilang mga ritwal.
Nakasuot pa rin ng kanilang mahahabang kasuotan ang mga pinuno.
Nakaupo pa rin ang hari sa kaniyang trono.
Pero sa ilalim ng lahat ng karangyaan… unti-unti nang namamatay ang Juda.
At sa loob mismo ng palasyo, isang natatakot na hari ang palihim na naghahanap sa propetang matagal na niyang hindi sinusunod.
Hindi lang ito kuwento tungkol sa isang mahinang hari.
Ito ang kuwento ng bawat taong alam na ang katotohanan… pero takot sa magiging kapalit ng pagsunod.
“At ipinatawag ni haring Zedekias si Jeremias na propeta… at sinabi ng hari kay Jeremias, ‘May itatanong ako sa iyo; huwag kang maglihim sa akin ng anuman.’”
Mabigat ang talatang iyon kapag talagang naunawaan mo.
Dahil hindi tinanong ni Zedekias si Jeremias sa harap ng bayan.
Malayo sa mga taong nakakaimpluwensya sa kaniya.
Gusto niya ang katotohanan… pero ayaw niya ng kahihiyan.
Gusto niya ang tinig ng Diyos… pero ayaw niya ng kabuuang pagsunod.
At milyon-milyon pa rin ang gumagawa nito hanggang ngayon.
May mga taong lihim na umiiyak habang nananalangin gabi-gabi pero buong araw ay nagpapanggap na okay lang sila.
May mga taong alam na nilang mali ang kanilang relasyon pero ayaw nilang bitawan.
May mga taong alam nang unti-unti silang sinisira ng kasalanan pero pinipili pa rin nilang manatili rito.
May mga taong matagal nang kinakausap ng Diyos… pero mas takot sila sa opinyon ng tao kaysa sa utos ng Panginoon.
Dito nagiging personal ang kuwento ni Zedekias.
Malaki ang pagkakaiba ng dalawang iyon.
“Kung ikaw ay lalabas… mabubuhay ka, at ang lungsod na ito ay hindi susunugin sa apoy.”
Kahit sa gitna ng paghatol… nag-aalok pa rin ang Diyos ng awa.
Kahit paulit-ulit na nilang binale-wala ang babala.
Patuloy pa ring sinasabi ng Diyos:
Dahil kayang gawing duwag ng takot sa tao kahit ang isang hari.
Iyan ang ugat ng kaniyang trahedya.
Nangangahulugan itong mabuhay sa matinding takot o pangamba.
At dahil mas natakot siya sa tao kaysa sa Diyos… nawala sa kaniya pareho.
Ito mismo ang babala sa Kawikaan 29:25:
“Ang takot sa tao ay nagdadala ng silo.”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “silo” ay:
Tahimik na lubid na unti-unting sumasakal.
Hindi nagsimula ang pagkawasak ni Zedekias nang bumagsak ang Jerusalem.
Matagal na siyang bihag sa loob.
At may mga taong nagbabasa nito ngayon na alam mismo ang pakiramdam na iyon.
Alam mong kinakausap ka na ng Diyos.
Pero takot kang mawalan ng mga tao.
Takot kang maging seryoso kay Cristo.
Kaya ginagawa mong lihim ang Diyos.
Paulit-ulit niyang hinahanap si Jeremias nang palihim habang tumatanggi pa ring lubusang sumunod sa Diyos.
At dumating ang araw na naubos ang oras.
Pinatay sa harap niya ang kaniyang mga anak.
Ang huling nakita niya ay paghatol.
Napakasakit isipin na hindi sana iyon kailangang mangyari.
Hindi siya napahamak dahil wala siyang narinig na katotohanan.
Napahamak siya dahil paulit-ulit niyang narinig ang katotohanan… pero ipinagpaliban niya ang pagsunod.
At iyan ang isa sa pinaka-mapanganib na kondisyon ng kaluluwa.
Ang paulit-ulit na pakikinig sa katotohanan nang walang pagsunod ay nagpapatigas ng puso.
Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον
“Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.”
Ay tumutukoy sa mga tagapakinig lamang.
Maraming tao ngayon ang parang si Zedekias.
Pero ayaw ng tunay na surrender.
Gusto nila ng comfort na walang repentance.
Pero ang tunay na Salita ng Diyos ay hindi lang nagbibigay-ginhawa.
“Sapagkat ang salita ng Diyos ay buhay at makapangyarihan, at higit na matalas kaysa alinmang tabak na may dalawang talim…”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “matalas” ay:
Inilalantad ng Salita ng Diyos ang mga bagay na pilit nating itinatago.
Kaya lihim na hinahanap ni Zedekias si Jeremias.
Dahil nanginginig ang mga nakatagong bagay kapag dumadating ang katotohanan.
At marahil kaya ito tumatama nang malalim sa puso mo ngayon.
Alam mo kung ano ang matagal nang kinukumbinsi sa iyo ng Diyos.
Alam mo kung saan nagsimula ang compromise.
Alam mo kung anong kasalanan ang pilit mong dine-depensa.
Alam mo kung anong surrender ang iniiwasan mo.
Handa pa ring magpatawad si Jesus.
Patuloy na nagbabala ang Diyos dahil mahal Niya ang tao.
“Ako’y walang kaluguran sa kamatayan ng masama; kundi ang masama ay manumbalik…”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “manumbalik” ay:
Ito ang puso ng tunay na pagsisisi.
At dito lalong nagiging napakaganda si Cristo.
Kung saan nabigo si Zedekias… nagtagumpay si Jesus.
Pero si Jesus ay lubos na sumunod sa Ama.
Itinago ni Zedekias ang sarili mula sa katotohanan.
Nabigo si Zedekias sa ilalim ng pressure.
Pero si Cristo ay nanatiling tapat hanggang kamatayan sa krus.
Ang Ebanghelyo ay hindi lang kuwento tungkol sa sinaunang hari.
Ito ay kuwento ng pagliligtas ng Diyos sa mga pusong unti-unti nang bumabagsak.
Si Jesus ang tumanggap ng hatol na para sana sa atin.
“Siya ay nasugatan dahil sa ating mga pagsalangsang…”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa “nasugatan” ay:
Si Cristo ang nasaktan upang makabalik ang mga makasalanan.
Kaya hindi kailangang magtapos ang kuwento mo gaya ng kay Zedekias.
Hindi mo kailangang manatiling lihim na naghahanap ng katotohanan habang patuloy na lumalaban sa Diyos.
Maaari kang sumuko kay Cristo ngayon.
Dahil ang ipinagpapalibang pagsunod ay pagsuway pa rin.
Pero habang may hininga… may awa pa.
May mga taong isang katotohanan na lang ang layo mula sa pagsuko kay Jesus.
Balang araw… ang mga lihim na pakikipaglaban ng puso mo ay makikita rin sa direksyon ng buhay mo.
